2607.09218.title: Tactile and Vision Conditioned Contact-Centric Control for Whole-Arm Manipulation
2607.09218.paper_summary: Whole-arm manipulation involves direct contact with the environment while the robot completes a task by distributing contact across multiple links as contacts form, slide, and break. This setting breaks common implicit assumptions in many learning-based manipulation pipelines: arm configuration tightly couples motion and contact forces, contact state is partially observed under occlusion, and purely learned rollouts can become physically inconsistent under distribution shift because many multi-link contact configurations are sparsely represented in the data. To address this, we propose TACTIC (Tactile and Vision Conditioned Contact-Centric Control), a receding-horizon controller for whole-arm manipulation. TACTIC uses a contact-centric hybrid predictive model that combines RGB-D, distributed tactile sensing, and a compact 2D proximity representation. The model couples a learned, action-conditioned latent dynamics model with analytical kinematics through contact Jacobians, enabling rollouts of future contact configurations and interaction forces. TACTIC integrates these rollouts into a sampling-based MPC planner with contact-aware action sampling: contact Jacobian-based projections steer sampled action sequences toward force-modulating directions, and objectives defined over predicted proximity and interaction forces trade task progress against whole-arm force regulation. We evaluate TACTIC in simulation against state-of-the-art model-based and model-free methods, and perform ablations that isolate the contribution of each design choice. TACTIC consistently outperforms other methods. We further demonstrate real-world performance on a robot with distributed tactile sensing across three whole-arm manipulation tasks that require multi-contact trajectories: turning over and repositioning a manikin, and goal-reaching in a 3D dynamic maze. Website: https://emprise.cs.cornell.edu/tactic
2607.09218.paper_summary_zh: 整臂操作涉及與環境的直接接觸，同時機器人通過在多個連接點之間分配接觸來完成任務，隨著接觸的形成、滑動和斷開。這種設置打破了許多基於學習的操作流程中的常見隱含假設：臂的配置緊密地將運動與接觸力耦合，接觸狀態在遮擋下部分可觀察，並且純學習的展開在分佈變化下可能變得物理上不一致，因為許多多連接接觸配置在數據中稀疏表示。為了解決這個問題，我們提出了TACTIC（觸覺和視覺條件接觸中心控制），這是一種用於整臂操作的回退視野控制器。TACTIC使用一種以接觸為中心的混合預測模型，該模型結合了RGB-D、分佈式觸覺感知和緊湊的2D接近表示。該模型通過接觸雅可比矩陣將學習的、以行動為條件的潛在動力學模型與解析運動學耦合，從而實現未來接觸配置和相互作用力的展開。TACTIC將這些展開集成到基於採樣的MPC規劃器中，並進行接觸感知的行動採樣：基於接觸雅可比矩陣的投影引導採樣的行動序列朝向力調節的方向，並且在預測的接近和相互作用力上定義的目標在任務進展與整臂力調節之間進行權衡。我們在模擬中評估TACTIC，與最先進的基於模型和無模型的方法進行比較，並進行消融實驗以隔離每個設計選擇的貢獻。TACTIC始終優於其他方法。我們進一步展示了在一個具有分佈式觸覺感知的機器人上，在三個需要多接觸軌跡的整臂操作任務中的實際表現：翻轉和重新定位一個人形模型，以及在3D動態迷宮中達到目標。網站：https://emprise.cs.cornell.edu/tactic
